title: Penile Doppler ultrasound
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to look at the blood vessels of the penis and how blood flows through them. Often an erection is brought on with medicine for this.
why: For erection problems, curvature, hard lumps, or after an injury.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes including waiting for the erection; the report is usually ready right away
tell_doctor: What medicines you take, especially blood thinners and blood pressure pills
If you took any erection medicine in the last 24 hours
If you ever had priapism, a long and painful erection

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually none. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: A normal shower the evening before or in the morning.

prepare.title: Erection medicines
prepare.text: Do not take them on your own the day before, unless your doctor said otherwise.

steps: You undress below the waist and lie on your back
First, the doctor checks the vessels at rest
Usually a small injection of medicine is given at the base of the penis to cause an erection
After a few minutes, the doctor checks blood flow again
The doctor measures the blood speed in the vessels
Before you leave, they check that the erection has gone down
feel: A thin needle prick, with brief pain
The erection from the medicine usually lasts a while and goes away by itself
It may feel awkward. It is a routine medical test, and the doctor is discreet
after: Do not leave until the erection goes down. This is standard
The report is usually ready right away
Go over the results with a urologist
red_flags: The erection lasts more than 4 hours or is very painful: go to hospital right away or call emergency services
Strong swelling or a large bruise at the injection site

faq.a: The needle is very thin, and the prick is quick. Most men say it is bearable.

faq.q: What if nerves stop the erection?
faq.a: The doctor can add a little more medicine or wait. Everyone gets nervous.

reminders.text: Penile Doppler tomorrow. Do not take erection medicines on your own. Bring a list of your medicines.
